sources.what: the usage object example (copied verbatim into documented_usage_example below), and the field meanings: 'cached_tokens is the number of tokens that were read from the cache'; 'cache_write_tokens is the number of tokens that were written to the cache (only returned for models with explicit caching and cache write pricing)'; 'cost: The total amount charged to your account'; 'Full usage details are now always included automatically in every response.'

the non-streaming Response and ResponseUsage types (id, choices[].message.{content,role,tool_calls}, finish_reason, native_finish_reason, created, model, object: 'chat.completion', usage.{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, prompt_tokens_details.{cached_tokens, cache_write_tokens}, completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens, cost, is_byok, cost_details.upstream_inference_cost}); and that `model` names the model that actually served the request
'OpenRouter uses a credit system where the base currency is US dollars. All of the pricing on our site and API is denoted in dollars.' — so usage.cost is read as USD
qwen/qwen3.8-flash lists tools + tool_choice, and prices prompt 0.00000015, completion 0.00000047, input_cache_read 0.000000016, input_cache_write 0.0000002 (USD per token)

_provenance.how_response_was_built: The `response` below is NOT a capture. It is built by the drafter to the documented ResponseUsage type, with non-zero cached_tokens AND cache_write_tokens so both mappings are exercised (the documented example has cached_tokens 0). Its `cost` is what the listed qwen/qwen3.8-flash prices give for these counts, assuming — as the documented example does (prompt_tokens 194 ⊇ cache_write_tokens 100) — that cache reads and cache writes are both PARTS of prompt_tokens: 2000 uncached x 0.15 + 9000 read x 0.016 + 1000 written x 0.2 + 800 output x 0.47, per million = 0.00102. That subset assumption is OPEN until the live smoke records a real response.
